subtitle: The Spear That Turned the South

panels.shot: epic low-angle mid-shot in the dust of battle
panels.action: Butuga II stands in battle armor on a smoky field, spear poised, a fallen banner behind him hinting at a great army's collapse on the plains near Takkolam.

dialogue.text: At Takkolam, c.949, Ganga king Butuga II rides for Rashtrakuta glory; one strike against Chola prince Rajaditya will bend the fate of south Indian empires.

i18n.hi: तक्कोलम, लगभग ९४९। गंगा नरेश बुटुगा द्वितीय राष्ट्रकूट यश के लिए दौड़ता है; चोल युवराज राजादित्य पर एक वार, दक्षिणी साम्राज्यों की किस्मत मोड़ देता है।

panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of peninsular India shows different colored banners over the Kaveri delta, the Deccan plateau, and the forests of Gangavadi, with faint arrows showing rival directions of expansion.

dialogue.text: In the mid-tenth century, the south groaned with ambition. The Cholas rose from the Kaveri, the Rashtrakutas ruled the Deccan, and the Western Gangas guarded their old hills of Gangavadi.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के बीचोंबीच, दक्षिण महत्त्वाकांक्षा से कराह उठा। कावेरी से चोल उठे, दक्कन पर राष्ट्रकूट छाए, और पश्चिमी गंगा अपने गंगावाड़ी पर्वतों की रखवाली करते रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot near a Jain basadi courtyard
panels.action: Young Butuga II, in simple yet noble attire, stands in a stone courtyard near a Jain basadi, elders around him, the distant outline of the hills of Gangavadi behind.

dialogue.text: Butuga, son of the Ganga house, grew amid stone basadis, warrior codes and shifting overlords. His forefathers had long balanced between mightier neighbours, yielding tribute yet guarding their hill country.

i18n.hi: गंगा वंशज बुटुगा पत्थर के बसदियों, योद्धा संहिताओं और बदलते स्वामियों के बीच पला। उसके पुरखे बलवान पड़ोसियों के बीच संतुलन रखते, कर देते, पर अपने पहाड़ी देस की पहरेदारी भी करते रहे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot in a Rashtrakuta court tent
panels.action: Butuga II stands before an unseen Rashtrakuta emperor inside a richly furnished war pavilion, his head bowed, right hand on the hilt of his sword, Rashtrakuta banners visible behind.

dialogue.text: By the 940s, Butuga had bound his destiny to the Rashtrakuta emperor Krishna III. As feudatory and ally, he took their banner, their campaigns, and their enemies as his own.

i18n.hi: ९४० के दशक तक बुटुगा ने अपनी नियति राष्ट्रकूट सम्राट कृष्ण तृतीय से जोड़ दी। सामंत और साथी बनकर, उसने उनका ध्वज, उनके रण और उनके शत्रु अपने मान लिए।

panels.shot: wide map-like shot morphing into marching armies
panels.action: An artistic blend of a palm-leaf map and real terrain shows Rashtrakuta-Ganga troops marching south, while Chola forces mass near the Kaveri, the two streams converging toward Takkolam.

dialogue.text: To the south, Parantaka I of the Cholas pushed northward, claiming lands long contested. In the northern Tamil country, near Takkolam, the two currents of power finally rushed toward each other.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में चोल राजा परांतक प्रथम उत्तर की ओर धकेलता गया, पुरानी विवादित भूमियाँ माँगता हुआ। उत्तरी तमिल देस में, तक्कोलम के पास, दो शक्तियों की धाराएँ आमने‑सामने आ टकराईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of an armored Chola prince on an elephant
panels.action: A Chola crown prince, Rajaditya, sits in ceremonial armor atop a war elephant, banners with the Chola tiger around him, the Kaveri plain stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: Parantaka’s chosen spearhead was his son Rajaditya. Chola inscriptions remember him as a brave prince, leading from the elephant howdah, his armour bright in the Kaveri sun.

i18n.hi: परांतक का चुना हुआ शस्त्र उसका पुत्र राजादित्य था। चोल शिलालेख उसे साहसी राजकुमार कहते हैं, हाथी की हौदा से सेना लीड करता, कवच कावेरी की धूप में दमकता।

panels.shot: tight medium shot in camp at night
panels.action: By firelight in a night camp, Butuga II sits polishing his spear, armor laid beside him, while shadowy outlines of horses and soldiers rest in the background.

dialogue.text: Somewhere to the north of Takkolam, Butuga’s camp fires burned. The Atakur inscription, carved soon after, would remember this campaign as the proving ground of his loyalty and courage.

i18n.hi: तक्कोलम के उत्तर कहीं बुटुगा के डेरा‑अलाव जल रहे थे। थोड़ी ही देर बाद खुदा आतकूर लेख इस मुहिम को उसकी निष्ठा और वीरता की अग्नि‑परीक्षा कहेगा।

panels.shot: close-up on Butuga II's face at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, Butuga II, now armoured, looks toward the horizon, his expression steady, dust rising as troops form behind him under Rashtrakuta and Ganga standards.

dialogue.text: Dawn at Takkolam, c.948–949. Fields near the village filled with cavalry and infantry. Rashtrakuta and Ganga lines formed under one command; Chola ranks waited behind their prince.

i18n.hi: तक्कोलम की भोर, लगभग ९४८–९४९। गाँव के खेत घुड़सवार और पैदल से भर उठे। राष्ट्रकूट और गंगा पंक्तियाँ एक ही कमान तले सजीं; चोल दल अपने राजकुमार के पीछे प्रतीक्षा में।

panels.shot: broadside wide shot of two armies facing each other
panels.action: Two dense battle lines face one another on a dry plain, elephants and horsemen in front, infantry in the rear, dust hanging in the air as conches blow.

dialogue.text: This was no holy war. It was a struggle for tribute, for frontier villages, for the right to command other chiefs. Yet for each man in the line, it was also about honour, pay and survival.

i18n.hi: यह कोई धर्मयुद्ध नहीं था। यह लगान के लिए, सरहदी गाँवों के लिए, और दूसरे सरदारों पर हुक्म चलाने के हक के लिए लड़ाई थी। पर हर सिपाही के लिए यह इज़्ज़त, मज़दूरी और जान की बाज़ी भी थी।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot alongside charging cavalry
panels.action: Butuga II rides at the head of a wedge of Ganga cavalry, spear lowered, his horse mid-gallop as his men surge forward into swirling dust and looming elephants.

dialogue.text: When the signal came, Butuga led a fierce cavalry charge for his Rashtrakuta overlord. The Atakur record praises him as the one who broke into the heart of the Chola formation.

i18n.hi: संकेत मिलते ही बुटुगा ने अपने राष्ट्रकूट स्वामी के लिए घुड़सवारों का भीषण धावा बोला। आतकूर लेख उसे वह कहता है जिसने चोल व्यूह के सीने पर सीधा वार किया।

panels.shot: medium shot from ground level showing elephant and horse converging
panels.action: From low angle, a Chola elephant bearing an armored prince towers ahead while Butuga II on horseback closes in through the chaos, spear pointed upward toward the howdah.

dialogue.text: Chola accounts remember Rajaditya on his elephant, leading in person. Kannada verses, carved in stone, claim that Butuga rode straight for that towering beast.

i18n.hi: चोल कथाएँ राजादित्य को हाथी पर, खुद आगे‑आगे बताते हैं। पत्थर पर खुदी कन्नड़ कविताएँ दावा करती हैं कि बुटुगा सीधे उस विराट हाथी पर टूट पड़ा।

panels.shot: tight action freeze on Butuga's spear thrust
panels.action: In a frozen instant, Butuga II thrusts his spear upward toward the silhouetted figure on the elephant, his face set with grim resolve as dust and motion blur around.

dialogue.text: In that brief, terrible moment, Butuga’s spear found its mark. Later inscriptions credit him with striking down Rajaditya, the Chola crown prince, before the armies locked again.

i18n.hi: उस क्षणिक, भयावह घड़ी में बुटुगा की भाला लक्ष्य पर बैठ गई। बाद के लेख उसे चोल युवराज राजादित्य को गिराने का श्रेय देते हैं, ठीक तब जब सेनाएँ फिर से भिड़ीं।

panels.shot: wide shot showing confusion in Chola ranks
panels.action: Chola soldiers in the foreground falter and look back in dismay as their war elephant sags and its banner tilts, while distant Rashtrakuta-Ganga troops press forward.

dialogue.text: With their prince fallen, the Chola battle line wavered. Rashtrakuta and Ganga forces surged, and the field at Takkolam belonged, for that day, to Krishna III and his allies.

i18n.hi: युवराज ढहते ही चोल पंक्ति डगमगाई। राष्ट्रकूट और गंगा सेनाएँ लहर की तरह चढ़ गईं, और तक्कोलम का मैदान उस दिन कृष्ण तृतीय और उसके साथियों के नाम हो गया।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of the battlefield after the fight
panels.action: The battlefield after combat shows abandoned shields, broken chariots and elephants being led away, as crows circle and distant soldiers gather their wounded and dead.

dialogue.text: The cost lay silent on the ground. For the Rashtrakuta empire, Takkolam opened the way deeper into the south. For the Cholas, it was a searing loss that checked their advance for years.

i18n.hi: क़ीमत ज़मीन पर निःशब्द पसरी थी। राष्ट्रकूट साम्राज्य के लिए तक्कोलम ने दक्षिण में और भीतर जाने का मार्ग खोला। चोलों के लिए यह ऐसा घाव था जिसने बरसों तक उनकी बढ़त रोक दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a stonecutter carving an inscription
panels.action: A stonecutter in a small village carefully chisels Kannada letters into a tall slab, villagers watching as he shapes a warrior figure and a dog in relief beneath the script.

dialogue.text: Yet the memory of Takkolam was not kept only in royal boasts. Near Atakur in present-day Karnataka, artisans prepared a hero-stone, its Kannada lines telling of Butuga’s deeds and a very different hero.

i18n.hi: पर तक्कोलम की याद सिर्फ़ शाही शेख़ी में नहीं बची। आज के कर्नाटक में आतकूर के पास शिल्पियों ने एक वीरगली गढ़ी, जिसकी कन्नड़ पंक्तियाँ बुटुगा की कथाएँ और एक बिलकुल अलग नायक उकेरती हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on carved relief of dog and boar on the hero-stone
panels.action: A close view of the Atakur-style hero-stone shows a detailed carved dog leaping at a wild boar, the two locked in struggle below the inscription lines.

dialogue.text: That inscription, while praising Butuga for felling Rajaditya at Takkolam, also honours Kali, a dog who died attacking a boar. The same stone world carried both imperial war and a hound’s courage.

i18n.hi: यह लेख, तक्कोलम में राजादित्य को गिराने वाले बुटुगा की प्रशंसा के साथ‑साथ काली नाम के उस कुत्ते का भी मान करता है जो सूअर पर झपटते हुए मारा गया। उसी पत्थर जगत में साम्राज्य‑युद्ध और एक शिकारी कुत्ते की हिम्मत दोनों दर्ज हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Butuga II at a dedication ceremony
panels.action: Butuga II, older and robed in royal finery, stands before a newly raised hero-stone in a rural setting, priests and warriors around him, his gaze thoughtful.

dialogue.speaker: butuga_ii
dialogue.text: Stones will speak when we are gone. Let them tell what we dared.

i18n.hi: हम चले जाएँगे, पत्थर बोलते रहेंगे। उन्हें कहना दो, हमने क्या दाँव खेला।

panels.shot: montage wide shot of inscriptions in different scripts and sites
panels.action: A visual montage shows Chola Tamil inscriptions on temple walls, Rashtrakuta records on rock, and the Kannada Atakur stone, all juxtaposed like a silent chorus of differing voices.

dialogue.text: Chola records mourned Rajaditya’s fall yet kept their pride. Rashtrakuta texts boasted of Krishna’s victory. The Atakur stone raised Butuga’s name, joining these voices in a layered, contested memory.

i18n.hi: चोल अभिलेखों ने राजादित्य की मृत्यु पर शोक किया, पर अपना मान बनाए रखा। राष्ट्रकूट ग्रंथों ने कृष्ण की विजय का डंका पीटा। आतकूर की गली ने बुटुगा का नाम ऊँचा किया, इन सब सुरों को मिलाकर एक उलझी, टकराती याद गढ़ी।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Butuga II's statue-like silhouette against hills
panels.action: Silhouetted against the hills of Gangavadi and distant Jain shrines, a statue-like image of Butuga II holding a spear stands timeless, the land around him fading into a map of south India.

dialogue.text: Today, we know Butuga II mostly through such stones. One spear thrust at Takkolam echoed through dynasties, reminding us how a single decision on a dusty plain can turn the course of empires.

i18n.hi: आज हम बुटुगा द्वितीय को ज़्यादातर ऐसी ही गलियों से जानते हैं। तक्कोलम में उसकी एक भाला‑चोट राजवंशों में गूँजती रही, बताती हुई कि धूल भरे मैदान पर एक फैसला भी साम्राज्यों की राह मोड़ सकता है।
